environment.description: Same Flask application deployed identically on EC2 behind ALB. The target group has the same configuration. However, the VPC uses AWS Network Firewall with a stateful rule group containing Suricata-compatible rules. The rule group includes a custom domain-list rule and a pass/drop policy. Additionally, the EC2 instance has an iptables NFQUEUE configuration with a userspace inspection daemon (using libnetfilter_queue) that performs protocol-level normalization on HTTP query strings before they reach the container's network namespace. The daemon applies RFC 3986 percent-decoding normalization and then matches decoded query parameter values against a pattern set. The pattern set includes signatures for SQL syntax tokens: any query parameter value containing a decoded sequence matching the regex `('|--|;|UNION\s|SELECT\s|INSERT\s|DROP\s|UPDATE\s|DELETE\s|OR\s+\d|AND\s+\d)` (case-insensitive) causes the packet to be dropped with a TCP RST. The NFQUEUE daemon operates at queue number 0 with a copy-range of 65535 bytes, ensuring full packet payload inspection. The iptables rule is: `iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j NFQUEUE --queue-num 0 --queue-bypass`. Note: --queue-bypass means if the daemon is not running, packets pass through.

config.runtime: Docker container on EC2 (Amazon Linux 2023), host network mode
config.network: ALB -> Target Group (port 8080), AWS Network Firewall in VPC
config.nfqueue_daemon: libnetfilter_queue userspace daemon on queue 0, copy-range 65535
config.inspection_logic: RFC 3986 percent-decode all query param values, then regex match case-insensitive: ('|--|;|UNION\s|SELECT\s|INSERT\s|DROP\s|UPDATE\s|DELETE\s|OR\s+\d|AND\s+\d) -> DROP+RST
config.daemon_status: systemd unit nfqueue-inspector.service, enabled, running, WatchdogSec=5, Restart=always
config.network_firewall_rules: Stateful Suricata rule group with HTTP protocol anomaly detection
